slots.note: Symmetrical box camera with knobs, viewfinder hood and a ringed lens, no markings; cropped to drop the cast shadow. 10100 had a lettering-like smudge, 10101 a shadow blob, 10102 a stray background strip.

All four teapots rejected (two-handled sugar bowls, fake script, a letter t). Backup coffee pot in side view: one spout, one handle; cast shadow painted out before oneink. 10253 stopped as not needed.
Front view, rimmed lenses in a padded mask, strap above and below (the lower band not visibly joined; reads a little like a face). Others: sunglasses, flat dark lenses, shadow blobs.

All four nib images were whole pens or rods, never a nib. The quill backup (started minute 84) gave four smooth white or half-black blades on black sticks with no barbs, one with fake lettering on the shaft: all rejected. Slot empty.
Engraving-like ball of laid rope with an eye and a tail, whole on the page; not a true monkey's fist, so titled ROPE KNOT (truth rule). Category Engravings (the one allowed).

lessons: Objects come out as photographs, but line mode turns them into usable screened line art; crop or paint out cast shadows first. 'Front view' of a pot gives two symmetrical handles and no spout: ask for side view. A 'nib close up' gives a whole pen. Queue a backup with a wait loop that cannot match its own command line (pgrep -f matched itself). A single feather fails again (smooth blade, no barbs): avoid feathers and quills for this model.
